extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies, power plant owners/operators, environmental regulators, environmental law practitioners, and other stakeholders affected by CAA §111 NSPS/Emission Guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule establishing New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) for new/modified/reconstructed fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs) and Emission Guidelines for existing fossil fuel-fired EGUs, including requirements for state plans, monitoring, compliance, and BSER determinations under Clean Air Act section 111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of the BSER for the source category as required under CAA section 111, including consideration of what system of emission reduction is 'best' for the source category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BSER determination addresses components such as system of emission reduction, adequacy demonstration, costs, non-air quality health and environmental impacts and energy requirements, sector or nationwide factors, 'best' meaning, amount of emissions reductions, promotion of technology development and implementation, and achievability of degree of emission limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequately Demonstrated
rubrics_metrics.description: "Adequately demonstrated" criterion for technologies/systems proposed as BSER, evaluated using plain text, statutory context, legislative history, caselaw, and compliance timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA assesses demonstration via real-world project examples, vendor statements, user statements, industrial applications, capture/transport/sequestration demonstrations (for CCS), permitting and rights-of-way experience, and other evidence that the technology can work at the scale and conditions of the source category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs (Cost Reasonableness and Comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of costs associated with candidate BSERs (capture, transport, sequestration, total costs), including comparison to other controls and measures of cost reasonableness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes consideration of IRC Section 45Q tax credit impacts, historical cost comparisons from prior rulemakings, and total cost calculations for options such as CCS or hydrogen; costs inform BSER and degree of limitation determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Air Quality Health and Environmental Impacts and Energy Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of non-air quality health/environmental impacts and energy requirements associated with candidate BSERs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically considers energy penalties, non-GHG emissions, water use, capture plant siting impacts, transport and sequestration impacts, and broader impacts on the energy sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of Reductions in CO2 Emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of how much CO2 (or GHG) emissions reduction a candidate BSER achieves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extent of reductions is used to support whether the system constitutes the 'best' system and to determine the degree of emission limitation in standards of performance or emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of the Development and Implementation of Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of whether adoption of a candidate BSER will promote further development and broader implementation of emissions-reducing technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA weighs whether regulation will encourage technology advancement, market transformation, and infrastructure development (e.g., CCS hubs, hydrogen supply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Achievability of the Degree of Emission Limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the degree of emissions limitation set by a standard is achievable in practice by affected sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers technical feasibility, resource and workforce availability to install controls, timing, and interactions with grid reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of Emission Limitation for Final Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification of the numerical or performance-based emission limits (degree of limitation) that will be final for affected subcategories (e.g., long-term coal, medium-term coal, natural gas-fired).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree of limitation derived from BSER determination and informed by cost, achievability, and expected emission reductions; includes separate treatment for subcategories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability Requirements and Fossil Fuel-Type Definitions for Subcategories
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria setting which units are covered (applicability) and definitions used to determine fossil fuel-type subcategories of steam generating units and turbines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for units permanently ceasing operation before compliance dates, sources outside contiguous U.S., IGCC units, and specific fossil-fuel type definitions shaping subcategorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategorization (Legal Basis and Metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing subcategories within the source category (e.g., long-term coal, medium-term coal, natural gas-fired; low/intermediate/base load combustion turbines) with legal basis and metrics such as electric sales or design efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains reasons for subcategorizing (differing BSERs/achievability/costs) and details on thresholds, higher heating value basis, load subcategories, multi-fuel units, CHP applicability, rural/small systems, and definitions of system emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of Performance for New and Reconstructed Units (Phase-1 and Phase-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance standards applicable to new and reconstructed stationary combustion turbines and steam generating units, including multi-phase standards where specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes base load, intermediate load, and low-load Phase-1 and Phase-2 standards, and the structure for phased implementation tied to BSER components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Modified Stationary Combustion Turbines and Steam Generating Units
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria determining when modifications trigger NSPS requirements and what standards apply to modified units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes definitions and applicability of Subpart TTTTa and criteria distinguishing modification/reconstruction/new construction; references to eight-year NSPS review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing and Monitoring Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: General and source-specific testing, monitoring, and compliance determination procedures to demonstrate standards attainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers general monitoring, emissions monitoring and reporting, CCS-specific monitoring and reporting, performance testing, and methods/equations to calculate standards (e.g., mass- or output-based equations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, Reports, and Records; Recordkeeping and Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific notification, reporting, and recordkeeping obligations for affected sources and for state plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes continuous monitoring system requirements (referencing 40 CFR part 75), notification timelines, required reports, records retention, and procedures for demonstrating compliance and transfers (e.g., CO2 transfer to entities reporting under GHGRP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Dates and Compliance Date Extension Mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance schedule(s) for standards (e.g., effective and compliance dates, special dates like January 2032 for certain measures) and mechanisms by which compliance dates may be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules allowing extensions, thresholds and procedures for extension, and interplay with state plan timelines and RULOF considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptive Standards and Baseline Emission Performance for State Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Presumptive standards and methods for establishing baseline emission performance that states may apply in their plans for affected steam generating units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses presumptive standards for long-term, medium-term, and natural gas/oil-fired units, baseline emission calculation methods, and application of presumptive standards in state plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for State Plans To Maintain Stringency of the EPA's BSER Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation that state-submitted plans implementing the emission guidelines maintain the stringency inherent in EPA's BSER determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may propose mechanisms but must demonstrate that plan achieves equivalent or more stringent outcomes consistent with BSER; EPA reviews and approves or disapproves state plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remaining Useful Life and Other Factors (RULOF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of a unit's remaining useful life and related factors when determining less-stringent standards or longer compliance schedules for particular units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes threshold requirements for invoking RULOF, methods for calculating standards that account for RULOF, invoking RULOF for long-term and medium-term coal units, contingency requirements, and interaction with other flexibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Flexibilities: Demonstrating Equivalent Stringency
rubrics_metrics.description: How sources or states may demonstrate equivalent stringency to the EPA's standard to employ alternative compliance pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies requirements for equivalency demonstrations, exclusions of certain affected EGUs from flexibilities, and criteria EPA will use to evaluate equivalency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Flexibilities: Rate-Based and Mass-Based Emission Trading and Averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms and standards for rate-based emission averaging and trading, unit-specific mass-based compliance, mass-based emission trading, interstate trading, and general program implementation features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details implementation features, accounting rules, eligibility, and how such programs interact with existing state programs and with EPA approval of state plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments of Progress and Reporting for EGUs Planning to Permanently Cease Operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for incremental progress milestones and reporting obligations for affected EGUs that plan to permanently cease operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies milestones, reporting timelines, and how such plans affect applicability, compliance schedules, and potential exclusion from some flexibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration and Requirements for CCS (Capture, Transport, and Geologic Sequestration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific evidentiary criteria and operational requirements used to evaluate CCS as BSER, including capture technology demonstrations, transport demonstrations, geologic sequestration availability and security, permitting, and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers examples of capture projects (e.g., Boundary Dam, Petra Nova), transport pipeline examples, trunklines, permitting and rights-of-way experience, UIC program interactions, Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program obligations, security of sequestration, and timing of permitting for sequestration sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options Considered but Not Determined To Be BSER
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment and rationale for technologies/options the EPA considered but did not select as BSER (e.g., partial capture CCS, natural gas co-firing, heat rate improvements, hydrogen co-firing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific reasons for non-selection such as inadequate demonstration, cost, energy impacts, or insufficient degree-of-limitation precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and Consideration of Low-GHG Hydrogen
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and considerations regarding low-GHG hydrogen including definitional approach, treatment of hydrogen production emissions, and whether low-GHG hydrogen is required for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses technological and market transformation considerations, infrastructure funding/tax incentives, EPA stakeholder engagement, and explanation for not requiring hydrogen used for compliance to be low-GHG hydrogen in this action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grid Reliability Considerations and Reliability-Related Mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses and mechanisms to evaluate and address electric grid reliability concerns associated with compliance (e.g., short-term reliability mechanism, reliability assurance mechanism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes considerations for reliability in setting compliance timelines, use of RULOF for reliability, potential reliability mechanisms, and EPA interactions with NERC/FERC analyses and emergency authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Justice Analytical Considerations and Outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and guidance for considering environmental justice in analytical work and for stakeholder outreach and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA describes analytical methods (proximity analyses, exposure analyses), outreach and engagement expectations, and how EJ considerations factor into regulatory impact and state plan review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications for Other CAA Programs (NSR, Title V)
rubrics_metrics.description: How the NSPS and emission guidelines interact with and affect other Clean Air Act programs such as New Source Review (NSR) and Title V permitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses control technology review implications for major NSR permits, NSR implications of NSPS and emission guidelines, and Title V program interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Plan Components, Submission Timing, and EPA Action on State Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Required components of state plans to implement emission guidelines, timing for submissions, provisions for plan revisions, dual-path standards, and how EPA will act on submitted plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies general and specific components (including meaningful engagement, transparency and compliance assurance), timing deadlines, revision processes, and federal plan applicability/promulgation timing if states fail to submit approvable plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic, Cost, and Benefit Analyses (Regulatory Impact Analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary and methods for assessing air quality impacts, compliance costs, economic and energy impacts, benefits and net benefits, and discounting approaches used in the rule's RIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of discount rates (e.g., 2%, 3%, 7%), social cost of greenhouse gases, modeling assumptions (IPM sensitivity), monetized climate benefits, and references to technical support documents and peer review materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Startup, Shutdown, and Malfunction (SSM) Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: How emissions during startup, shutdown, and malfunction events are addressed in standards, monitoring, and compliance determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes references to SSM provisions in standards and monitoring/recordkeeping expectations related to those operational periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equations, Tables, and Calculation Procedures for Emission Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific equations, tables, and calculation procedures included in regulatory text (e.g., Equation 1/2/3 to paragraphs, tables of CO2 emission standards for affected units).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These formulae and tables define mass- or output-based standards, applicability matrices, and methods for determining baseline emission rates and performance against standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Applicability (Units Outside Contiguous U.S., IGCC, Permanently Ceasing Units)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules and applicability distinctions for sources outside the contiguous U.S., IGCC units, and coal-fired units permanently ceasing operation before certain dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines how these categories are treated with respect to applicability, subcategorization, and potential exclusions or tailored compliance timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of Public Docketing, Supporting Documents, and Public Comment Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures related to the administrative record, docketing on Regulations.gov, and consideration of supporting documents and public comments in rationale and responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA maintains docket (EPA-HQ-OAR-2023-0072) with supporting documents (technical support documents, project examples, economic analyses) and responds to comments in preamble sections and appendices; some docket materials may be CBI or not publicly posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement and legal consideration about severability of action components if parts are invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses how remaining portions of the rule would operate if particular provisions are struck down or found unlawful.
